## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A one-fascicle Chinese rendering of the **Mūlasarvāstivāda *bhikṣuṇī-prātimokṣa*** (358 rules), drawn from the parent *Mūlasarvāstivāda Bhikṣuṇī-vibhaṅga* ([KR6k0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0024)). Translated by **Yìjìng** ([義淨](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%BE%A9%E6%B7%A8)) in the early 8th century. The Sanskrit text is preserved in the Gilgit manuscripts.

**Abstract**

The Mūlasarvāstivāda *bhikṣuṇī-prātimokṣa* is one of the four extant complete *bhikṣuṇī* rule-sets in the Chinese canon. Tsomo's (1996) comparative study of the Dharmaguptaka and Mūlasarvāstivāda *bhikṣuṇī* prātimokṣas is the standard reference. The pre-modern Tibetan tradition never established a *bhikṣuṇī* lineage, so this text — though canonical for Tibetan Buddhism — has no historic Tibetan ordination tradition. Recent ordination-revival movements have used the Dharmaguptaka *bhikṣuṇī*-prātimokṣa ([KR6k0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0012)) instead.
